title: ActionRoguelike's Action System: URogueActionComponent, URogueAction and URogueAttributeSet
intro: You'll be able to trace how URogueActionComponent ties together URogueAction, URogueActionEffect and URogueAttributeSet. That covers how URogueGameplayFunctionLibrary::ApplyDamage becomes a Health change, how URogueActionEffect_Thorns and URogueActionEffect_StunFromDamage react to it, and how the server and clients stay in sync. You'll also know where to add a new attribute or effect.
subject: The action system: how actions, effects and attributes work together
materialNote: README lists the Action System only as a feature bullet and still mentions an AttributeComponent that no longer exists. The tutorial relies on the code in Source/ActionRoguelike/ActionSystem.

chapters.title: RogueActionComponent.cpp: the hub that owns Actions and the AttributeSet
chapters.goal: Explain, from RogueActionComponent.h and RogueActionComponent.cpp, what URogueActionComponent owns (Actions, CachedActions, AttributeSet, ActiveGameplayTags, DefaultActions), how BeginPlay grants DefaultActions on the server, and how StartActionByName finds an action by ActivationTag.
chapters.hootIntro: Every actor that fights in ActionRoguelike carries one URogueActionComponent, and this chapter shows what that hub holds and how it dispatches actions.

steps.title: One component per actor, in Source/ActionRoguelike/ActionSystem
steps.body: The action system lives in `Source/ActionRoguelike/ActionSystem`, and `URogueActionComponent` is its hub. It is an `UActorComponent` marked `BlueprintSpawnableComponent`, so players and monsters get it as a component. It holds three things: the actions an actor can perform (`URogueAction`), the actor's numbers (a `URogueAttributeSet`), and a set of gameplay tags describing its current state. Other code finds it from any actor through `URogueActionComponent::GetActionComponent`, which just forwards to `URogueGameplayFunctionLibrary`.

sources.why: Class declaration and the public action API
GetActionComponent delegates to the function library

steps.title: Walking the component's state in the header

stops.annotation: `ActiveGameplayTags` is the actor's current status, a `Transient` `FGameplayTagContainer`. Actions add tags here while running, and `GetActiveTags` exposes it.
`AttributeSet` is an `Instanced` `URogueAttributeSet` that can be swapped per actor (Health, MoveSpeed, ...). It replicates and calls `OnRep_AttributeSet` on clients.

`DefaultActions` is the designer-edited list of classes granted at start. `Actions` holds the live instances and is replicated. `CachedActions` is a non-replicated map from `FGameplayTag` to action, used for quick lookups.

steps.question: `Actions` is replicated but `CachedActions` is not. How does a client end up with a usable `CachedActions` map?
choices: OnRep_Actions clears and rebuilds it from Actions, keyed by each ActivationTag
It is copied across the network by a Server RPC
Each client builds it in BeginPlay from DefaultActions
It is saved to disk and loaded by the save game system
steps.hint: Look at the RepNotify declared next to the Actions property and at its body near the end of the .cpp.
steps.explanation: `OnRep_Actions` runs on clients when the array arrives, empties `CachedActions` and re-adds every action under `GetActivationTag()`. The host does the same work inside `AddAction`/`RemoveAction`, so the map never needs to travel over the network.

steps.title: InitializeComponent guarantees an AttributeSet
steps.body: `InitializeComponent` runs before `BeginPlay`. If no `AttributeSet` was assigned (via `SetDefaultAttributeSet` in an actor constructor or in the Blueprint details panel), it creates a bare `URogueAttributeSet` and logs a warning naming the owner. It then calls `InitAttributeSet`, which fills the tag-keyed attribute cache. On the server it registers the set with `AddReplicatedSubObject`. The nullptr check deliberately sits before `Super::` because of an engine check on double initialization.

sources.why: SetDefaultAttributeSet is only allowed during init

steps.title: Where DefaultActions become server-only
steps.prompt: Click the line that restricts granting DefaultActions to the server.
steps.explanation: `GetOwner()->HasAuthority()` gates the loop that calls `AddAction` for each entry of `DefaultActions`. Clients get their `Actions` array through replication rather than creating their own copies.

steps.title: StartActionByName, step by step
steps.prompt: Put the path of StartActionByName in order, as it runs on the server.
items: Find the action in CachedActions using the ActionName tag
Check whether the owner has authority
steps.explanation: The tag is the key into `CachedActions`. A client does not run the action but forwards `ServerStartAction` and lets the server judge `CanStart`. On the server, a failed `CanStart` prints an on-screen message and returns false. Otherwise `StartAction` runs.

steps.title: Find every user of CachedActions
steps.instruction: In your IDE, run Find All References on `CachedActions` in `RogueActionComponent.cpp`. Compare the hits with `AddAction`, `RemoveAction`, `StartActionByName` and `OnRep_Actions`, and note which ones write to the map and which only read it.
steps.expected: Writes in AddAction, RemoveAction and OnRep_Actions. A read in StartActionByName.

sources.why: Cache writes in AddAction and RemoveAction

takeaways: URogueActionComponent owns Actions, CachedActions, AttributeSet, ActiveGameplayTags and the DefaultActions list.
BeginPlay grants DefaultActions only when HasAuthority, and InitializeComponent guarantees an AttributeSet exists.
StartActionByName looks up CachedActions by ActivationTag and forwards to ServerStartAction on clients.

chapters.title: URogueAction lifecycle: CanStart, GrantsTags, BlockedTags and cooldown
chapters.goal: Describe the URogueAction lifecycle (CanStart, StartAction, StopAction) and how GrantsTags, BlockedTags and CooldownUntil gate it, using URogueAction_ProjectileAttack and the Status.* tags in DefaultGameplayTags.ini as examples.

chapters.title: RogueAttributeSet.h: FRogueAttribute, Base vs Modifier and ApplyAttributeChange
chapters.goal: Explain, from RogueAttributeSet.h and RogueGameplayFunctionLibrary.cpp, how FRogueAttribute combines Base and Modifier in GetValue, how FillAttributeCache builds the 'Attribute.<VarName>' tag map, and how ApplyAttributeChange, PostAttributeChanged and ApplyDamage drive the Health attribute set.

chapters.title: RogueActionEffect.cpp: Duration, Period, stacking, Thorns and StunFromDamage
chapters.goal: Show, from RogueActionEffect.cpp, RogueActionEffect_Thorns.cpp and RogueActionEffect_StunFromDamage.cpp, how URogueActionEffect adds Duration, Period and StackCount to URogueAction, and how Thorns and StunFromDamage listen to Attribute.Health.

chapters.title: Replication in RogueActionComponent.cpp and RogueAction.cpp
chapters.goal: Explain, from RogueActionComponent.cpp, RogueAction.cpp and RogueAttributeSet.cpp, which parts run on the server only and what replicates: Actions, AttributeSet, Health via OnRep_Health, RepData and CooldownUntil. Also how ServerStartAction forwards client requests.
